figures.caption: Figure 1. All elements utilized in the doped LLZO samples made in the current study. Dopants studied previously (typically ionic conductivity only) are in blue, and new dopants reported for the ﬁrst time here are in yellow, with elements in the undoped in red. Herein, all the dopants (yellow and blue, except Sb) were tested and screened for not only ionic conductivity but we also systematically screened electronic conductivity, and stability window.

figures.caption: Figure 2. a) Representative XRD patterns of various doped LLZO samples showing pure cubic garnets, mixtures of cubic and tetragonal garnets, and samples that are multiphase including a non-garnet phase such as Li2ZrO3, La2Zr2O7, and SiO2 marked by *. b) Results of multiphase Rietveld ﬁts on the three Ga-doped samples.

figures.caption: Figure 5. Results of CVs for testing the high voltage stability limit of the LLZO samples with the carbonate-based electrolyte. All samples have dopants substituted on the theoretical optimum sites. For all scans, the blank values were subtracted such that the voltage window ends at the lowest voltage where current exceeds 0 mA g−1. The red arrows highlight examples of dopants that strongly suppress or increase the oxidation.
figures.src: 51. Comprehensive Dopant Screening in Li₇La₃Zr₂O₁₂ Garnet Solid Electrolyte.pdf

figures.caption: Figure 6. a) Results of CVs for testing the low voltage stability limit of the LLZO samples with the carbonate-based electrolyte. All samples have dopants substituted on the theoretical optimum sites. For all scans, the blank values were subtracted such that the voltage window ends at the highest voltage where current goes below 0 mA g−1. b–d) Results were obtained for the same test using ionic liquid electrolyte at 55 °C on a few selected dopants of high interest (in the black boxes in a). The stability window ends at the highest voltage where the LLZO signal dips below that of the blank.
